draft.title: Why businesses close
card: the owner decides to close, for example by retiring, selling the business or moving on to something else.
the business must close because it cannot pay its debts. Being unable to pay debts when they are due is called insolvency.
the legal process for an insolvent person, such as a sole trader. A trustee deals with their assets and debts.
the legal process for an insolvent company. A liquidator sells its assets to pay creditors, the people owed money.
draft.remember: Closing can be a choice or forced by insolvency. Bankruptcy is for people, liquidation for companies.

opts: Being unable to pay debts when they are due
Closing a business because the owner retires
Selling a business to another owner
Selling stock at a lower price to attract buyers
a.why: Insolvency means debts cannot be paid when due, which can force a business to close. Retiring is a choice to close and does not involve being unable to pay.
a.clue: It is about debts, not about the owner's wishes.

b.q: Hana's Hardware Pty Ltd is a company that owes more than it can pay. Its creditors apply to wind it up. Which legal process applies?
opts: Liquidation, because it is an insolvent company
Bankruptcy, because it owes money to creditors
Liquidation, because the owner chose to retire
Bankruptcy, because it is a small business
b.why: A company that cannot pay its debts goes through liquidation, where a liquidator sells assets to pay creditors. Bankruptcy is the tempting answer but applies to people, not companies.
b.clue: Check whether the debtor is a person or a company.

a.best: Being unable to pay debts when they are due

b.best: Liquidation, because it is an insolvent company

problems.detail: The clue 'It is about debts, not about the owner's wishes' nearly states the answer, so it gives it away.

a.best: Being unable to pay debts when they are due
